purpose: machine-facing knowledge base for finding, computing, normalizing, interpreting, validating, and responsibly reporting citation-based indicators and relational citation methods as a subdomain node of bibliometrics, scientometrics and research evaluation
assumptions: no observed citation dataset is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic planning priors
the parent domain is bibliometrics, scientometrics and research evaluation
this node serves a knowledge-searcher meta-KB about where and how to find, evaluate, and synthesize authoritative citation knowledge
indicators are computed for planning/evaluation, not for unconditioned ranking
key references: de Solla Price Little Science Big Science 1963; Moed Citation Analysis in Research Evaluation 2005; Ding Rousseau Wolfram Measuring Scholarly Impact 2014
exclusions: full-text content and citation-context machine reading at scale
research funding allocation mechanics beyond indicator validity
general network science not tied to citation relations

competency_questions.question: what counts as a citation versus a reference and which document types and units are admitted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CITE_SCOPE node defines unit, document types, and reference-vs-citation rule

competency_questions.question: which citation database or open data source fits the question given coverage, bias, and reproducibility needs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DB_SELECT and OPEN_DATA nodes plus their dependency edges resolve source choice

competency_questions.question: how are records deduplicated and authors/references disambiguated before counting?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEDUP_DISAMBIG node defines entity resolution outputs and gates

competency_questions.question: how are raw citation counts and citations-per-paper computed for the defined units?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RAW_COUNTS node defines count outputs and acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: which citation window applies and how does it interact with distribution shape?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CITE_WINDOW, RAW_COUNTS, DISTRIB_SKEW nodes and the mean-vs-percentile axis

competency_questions.question: how are fields delineated and which reference sets drive normalization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_DELIN and FIELD_NORM nodes and their dependency edge

competency_questions.question: how are indicators normalized for field, type, and year to compare across fields?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_NORM node and the raw-vs-normalization conflict axis

competency_questions.question: which composite or aggregate indicator (h-index, journal metrics) fits which unit and level?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HINDEX, JOURNAL_METRICS, AGG_LEVEL nodes and the level-consistency rule

competency_questions.question: how are self-citations and manipulation patterns detected and handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_CITE and GAMING_DETECT nodes and their edges

competency_questions.question: how is the heavy-tailed citation distribution characterized and reflected in summaries and comparisons?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTRIB_SKEW and BENCH_COMPARE nodes define diagnostics and intervals

competency_questions.question: how are co-citation and bibliographic coupling networks built and distinguished for science mapping?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COCITE and BIBCOUPLE nodes and their similarity edge

competency_questions.question: how is the whole analysis made reproducible and provenance-tracked from source to indicator?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPRO_PIPELINE node and the reporting workflow step

competency_questions.question: what does a citation count actually measure, and which theory frames its interpretation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CITE_THEORY and INDIC_VALIDITY nodes define interpretation and validity

competency_questions.question: how are indicators validated, responsibly used, and synthesized into a decision-aligned report?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDIC_VALIDITY and REPORT_SYNTH nodes plus risk-over-speed dominance

glossary.definition: a citation is an incoming acknowledgement (cited side); a reference is an outgoing entry in a document's list (citing side)
the time span over which citations to a set of documents are counted
the largest h such that h papers each have at least h citations
largest g such that the top g papers together have at least g squared citations
mean normalized citation score; citations divided by the field/type/year expected mean
the assignment of documents to fields/subfields that defines normalization reference sets
two documents co-cited when a later document references both; a cited-side relatedness measure
two documents coupled when they share references; a citing-side relatedness measure
a citation where citing and cited works share at least one author or journal
the heavy-tailed, right-skewed shape of citation distributions with many uncited items
San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment; bars journal metrics for individual evaluation
ten principles for responsible use of research metrics

evidence_label_policy.rule: all estimates use heuristic and reference SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR; observed_impact, data_quality, and observed_co_occurrence are 0.0 with no observed dataset

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for citation-analysis structure, indicators, risks, and workflow
grounding_limits: values are priors for planning, not measurements

nodes.definition: Define what counts as a citation versus a reference and fix the citing/cited units, document types, and counting rules before any indicator is computed.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corpus document-type policy or citing/cited unit definition changes

pros.example: counting outgoing references as impact inflates a review article's apparent influence
fixing citable-item types makes JIF and h-index comparable across runs

cons.claim: definitional choices are contested and value-laden
cons.example: whether to count proceedings as citable items changes CS rankings

cons.claim: document-type misclassification propagates silently
cons.example: an editorial miscoded as article distorts per-paper averages

acceptance_tests: reference vs citation distinction documented with examples
document-type inclusion list explicit and justified
revisit_triggers: corpus expanded to new document types
switch between citing-side and cited-side counting

nodes.definition: Select and characterize the citation data source (Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, OpenAlex) given coverage, indexing policy, and access constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a database changes indexing policy or a new source (e.g., OpenAlex release) shifts coverage

pros.example: WoS undercounts non-English and book-based fields versus Scopus/OpenAlex
recording the snapshot date lets a study be rerun

cons.claim: each source has structural coverage bias
cons.example: Scopus over-represents STEM serials; OpenAlex has noisier author disambiguation

cons.claim: cross-source merging introduces duplicates
cons.example: DOI-less records duplicate across WoS and Dimensions

acceptance_tests: known-bias register attached to source choice
revisit_triggers: coverage gap discovered in target field

nodes.definition: Deduplicate records and disambiguate authors, institutions, and cited references so citation links resolve to the correct entities.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when disambiguation algorithm or identifier coverage (ORCID adoption) changes materially

pros.claim: correct entity links are prerequisite for author-level metrics
pros.example: merging J. Smith variants prevents h-index fragmentation
matching cited-reference strings recovers links lost to typos

cons.claim: disambiguation errors bias author indicators
cons.example: over-merging inflates a common-name author's citation count

cons.claim: computationally expensive at scale
cons.example: pairwise reference matching is quadratic without blocking

acceptance_tests: disambiguation precision/recall estimated on a sample

nodes.definition: Compute raw citation counts and citations-per-paper for the defined units within a stated citation window.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when citation window or counting unit changes

pros.example: total citations of a paper can be recomputed from the link table
per-paper means feed normalization

cons.claim: means are dominated by skew and outliers
cons.example: one highly cited paper makes a group's mean unrepresentative

cons.claim: not comparable across fields or ages
cons.example: raw counts favor older biomedical papers over young math papers

failure_modes: reporting mean over a skewed distribution

nodes.definition: Choose and justify the citation window (fixed vs variable, length, and synchronous vs diachronous mode) for counting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when comparing cohorts of different ages or when citation accrual lag differs by field

pros.example: a 3-year window is fair for fast fields but truncates math citations
aligning windows lets 2019 and 2021 cohorts be compared

cons.claim: short windows penalize slow-citing fields
cons.example: a 2-year JIF undercounts mathematics impact

cons.claim: variable windows complicate reproducibility
cons.example: open-ended windows shift as the database updates

failure_modes: window too short for slow fields
acceptance_tests: window length justified against field citation-lag profile

nodes.definition: Normalize citation counts for field, document type, and publication year to enable cross-field comparison (e.g., MNCS, percentile-based indicators).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when field delineation scheme or reference set changes

pros.example: MNCS lets a math paper and a biology paper be compared on relative impact
top-10% share is robust to a single mega-cited paper

cons.claim: results depend heavily on field delineation
cons.example: reclassifying a journal changes a department's MNCS

cons.claim: mean-based normalization still sensitive to skew
cons.example: MNCS divides by a skewed field mean

acceptance_tests: percentile indicator reported alongside mean-based one

nodes.definition: Delineate fields/subfields using journal schemes, citation-based clustering, or hybrid approaches, which sets the reference sets for normalization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when switching between journal-based and citation-clustering field schemes

pros.claim: determines validity of all normalized indicators
pros.example: cluster-based fields capture interdisciplinary work better than journal categories

pros.claim: granularity can be tuned to question
pros.example: fine clusters separate subfields with different citation cultures

cons.claim: no scheme is neutral; assignments are contestable
cons.example: multi-category journals force arbitrary tie-breaks

cons.claim: clustering is sensitive to parameters and network snapshot
cons.example: resolution parameter changes cluster membership

failure_modes: coarse fields hiding subfield citation differences
acceptance_tests: scheme robustness checked across two methods

nodes.definition: Compute the h-index and its variants (g-index, m-quotient) for authors, groups, or journals, capturing combined productivity and impact.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when aggregation level changes or when database coverage of an author's corpus shifts

pros.claim: single number combining output and impact
pros.example: h=20 summarizes 20 papers each cited >=20 times

pros.claim: robust to a few uncited or mega-cited papers
pros.example: one 5000-citation paper does not inflate h beyond corpus size

cons.claim: insensitive to highly cited papers and field/age
cons.example: compresses a Nobel-level corpus and a steady one to similar h

cons.claim: not field- or career-length normalized
cons.example: senior biologists out-h young mathematicians by construction

acceptance_tests: g-index or m-quotient reported alongside h

nodes.definition: Detect and handle author-, co-author-, and journal-level self-citations and decide whether/how to adjust indicators.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when self-citation rate exceeds a field-typical threshold or integrity concern is raised

pros.claim: self-citation is partly legitimate, partly gameable
pros.example: building on one's prior work is normal; coercive self-citation is not
high journal self-citation can trigger JIF suppression review

cons.claim: blanket removal can distort legitimate cumulative work
cons.example: stripping all self-citations penalizes programmatic researchers

cons.claim: requires accurate authorship resolution
cons.example: misattributed authorship misclassifies self vs external citations

acceptance_tests: self-citation classification validated on a sample

nodes.definition: Characterize the heavy-tailed citation distribution (skewness, uncitedness, percentiles) to choose appropriate summary statistics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when distribution shape diagnostics indicate mean-based summaries are misleading

pros.example: showing the tail explains why median is preferred
bootstrap CIs reflect tail-driven instability

cons.claim: power-law claims are often statistically unsupported
cons.example: log-normal frequently fits citation tails as well or better

cons.claim: small samples make tail estimation unstable
cons.example: a department with 30 papers has an unreliable top-percentile estimate

failure_modes: asserting power law without fit testing
using mean on a skewed sample
acceptance_tests: distribution shape diagnosed before choosing summary statistic

nodes.definition: Build and interpret co-citation networks (documents, authors, journals) to map intellectual structure and research fronts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corpus time slice changes or clustering resolution is retuned

pros.claim: reveals intellectual base and emerging fronts
pros.example: co-citation clusters expose foundational works of a specialty
ACA positions schools of thought relative to each other

cons.claim: reflects past consensus, lags emerging work
cons.example: co-citation favors already-recognized references

cons.claim: sensitive to threshold and normalization choices
cons.example: co-citation strength normalization changes cluster boundaries

nodes.definition: Construct and interpret bibliographic coupling networks (shared references) to detect current, emerging relatedness between documents.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reference completeness or corpus recency changes

pros.claim: detects current relatedness immediately at publication
pros.example: coupling links two new papers sharing a reference base
coupling sees emerging clusters before they accrue citations

cons.claim: depends on reference-list completeness
cons.example: truncated reference parsing weakens coupling links

cons.claim: static once published; does not evolve
cons.example: a paper's coupling profile is fixed at publication

failure_modes: treating coupling as identical to co-citation
unnormalized coupling favoring long reference lists

nodes.definition: Apply citation theory (normative vs social-constructivist, citer motivations) to interpret what citation counts actually measure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when indicator results are used to make value judgments about quality or merit

pros.claim: prevents naive equation of citations with quality
pros.example: perfunctory and negative citations count the same as endorsements
Mertonian view justifies citations as peer recognition signal

cons.claim: theories are not mutually reconcilable
cons.example: normative and constructivist accounts disagree on what counts mean

cons.claim: motivation studies are hard to scale
cons.example: hand-coded citation context does not generalize to millions of links

acceptance_tests: interpretation frame names the assumed citation theory
validity caveats attached to count-based claims

nodes.definition: Compute and contextualize journal-level indicators (JIF, CiteScore, SJR, SNIP, Eigenfactor) and their proper scope of use.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when journal metrics are proposed for individual or article-level evaluation

pros.claim: useful for journal-level comparison and selection
pros.example: SNIP enables fairer cross-field journal comparison than raw JIF
Eigenfactor downweights self-citation and weights by source prestige

cons.claim: misused for individual/article evaluation (DORA)
cons.example: ranking a researcher by their journals' JIFs is invalid

cons.claim: JIF is skew-driven and window-sensitive
cons.example: a single highly cited article inflates a journal's JIF

revisit_triggers: journal metric proposed for individual evaluation
new journal indicator adopted by stakeholders

nodes.definition: Ensure indicators are computed and compared at a consistent, appropriate aggregation level (article, author, group, institution, country).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when results are inferred from one aggregation level to another

pros.example: journal-level JIF must not be used to judge an article
fractional counting fairly attributes hyper-authored papers

cons.claim: fractional counting is harder to interpret
cons.example: stakeholders expect whole-paper credit

cons.claim: level mixing is a common silent error
cons.example: aggregating author h-indices to a department is not meaningful

acceptance_tests: aggregation level explicit and constant within a comparison

nodes.definition: Integrate open citation data and infrastructures (OpenAlex, OpenCitations/COCI, Crossref) and assess their completeness against proprietary sources.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when open-source coverage improves or a proprietary source becomes inaccessible

pros.example: OpenAlex snapshots can be shared with a study

pros.claim: closes the gap with proprietary coverage over time
pros.example: Crossref reference deposits keep expanding open citation links

cons.claim: open reference completeness still lags in places
cons.example: closed-reference publishers leave gaps in COCI

cons.claim: metadata noise higher than curated sources
cons.example: OpenAlex author/affiliation noise needs extra cleaning

acceptance_tests: coverage-gap quantified against a proprietary baseline

nodes.definition: Assess construct validity of indicators and apply responsible-metrics principles (Leiden Manifesto, DORA) before evaluative use.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when indicators inform funding, hiring, promotion, or institutional ranking decisions

pros.example: DORA stops JIF from driving tenure decisions
Leiden Manifesto pairs metrics with expert assessment

cons.claim: principles are guidance, not algorithms
cons.example: DORA does not specify a replacement metric

cons.claim: responsible use slows demand for simple rankings
cons.example: stakeholders want a single league-table number

failure_modes: using metrics as sole evaluation basis
acceptance_tests: responsible-use statement attached to evaluative outputs

nodes.definition: Build a reproducible, versioned analysis pipeline capturing source snapshots, code, parameters, and indicator provenance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any source snapshot, parameter, or indicator definition changes

pros.example: a versioned snapshot lets reviewers reproduce every indicator

pros.claim: isolates the effect of methodological choices
pros.example: rerunning with a different window quantifies its impact

cons.claim: upfront engineering cost
cons.example: provenance logging adds pipeline overhead

cons.claim: snapshot storage can be large
cons.example: full database snapshots are costly to retain

acceptance_tests: full rerun reproduces published indicators within tolerance
provenance log covers sources, code, parameters

nodes.definition: Define benchmark/reference groups and statistical comparison procedures (uncertainty, stability intervals) for fair indicator comparison.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when small-group comparisons are presented as definitive rankings

pros.example: stability intervals show two departments are statistically tied
benchmark adjusts for group size when comparing output

cons.claim: stability-interval methods are not standardized
cons.example: different bootstrap choices yield different intervals

cons.claim: benchmarks can be gamed by group definition
cons.example: narrowing a benchmark flatters the target group

nodes.definition: Detect manipulation patterns (citation cartels, coercive/excessive self-citation, citation stacking) that distort indicators.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an indicator shows an anomalous jump inconsistent with field norms

pros.example: detecting a citation ring prevents a fraudulent ranking
dense reciprocal citing among a small group flags a cartel

cons.claim: high false-positive risk harms reputations
cons.example: legitimate tight-knit subfields look cartel-like

cons.claim: manipulators adapt to known detectors
cons.example: gamers spread citations to evade simple thresholds

failure_modes: acting on flags without human review
acceptance_tests: anomaly thresholds validated against known cases
every flag routed to human integrity review

nodes.definition: Synthesize indicators into a contextualized, caveat-bearing report aligned to the decision question and audience.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the decision question or audience changes the appropriate indicator set

pros.claim: aligns indicators to the actual decision
pros.example: reporting field-normalized percentiles, not raw counts, for cross-field panels
stating window and field limits stops over-interpretation

cons.claim: tailoring risks cherry-picking
cons.example: selecting only flattering indicators misleads

cons.claim: caveats can be ignored by readers
cons.example: decision-makers skip limitation sections

acceptance_tests: every reported indicator carries field/window/level caveats
indicator set justified against the decision question
revisit_triggers: audience changes from technical to policy

edges.why_related: database choice must serve the fixed citation-unit and document-type policy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns coverage to the counting unit
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a source before fixing units forces rework
edges.example: choosing WoS before deciding proceedings count wastes effort if CS is in scope
edges.resolution_rule: unit definition dominates; reselect source to fit units

edges.why_related: disambiguation operates on the chosen source's record structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: entity resolution tuned to source schema
edges.risk_of_conflict: cleaning before source is final wastes the work
edges.example: switching from Scopus to OpenAlex changes disambiguation inputs
edges.resolution_rule: fix source first; rerun disambiguation on the final source

edges.why_related: open-data integration is framed against the selected primary source's coverage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: positions open data as complement or replacement
edges.risk_of_conflict: integrating open data before source decision duplicates effort
edges.example: building an OpenAlex pipeline before choosing it as primary
edges.resolution_rule: selection decision governs whether open data is primary or supplementary

edges.why_related: the pipeline must capture the chosen source's snapshot and access path
edges.benefit_of_coupling: provenance keyed to the actual source
edges.risk_of_conflict: building the pipeline before source choice forces refactor
edges.example: hardcoding WoS API then switching to Scopus
edges.resolution_rule: source choice fixes the pipeline data-ingestion layer

edges.why_related: window policy applies to the fixed citing/cited units
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing a window before units invites mismatch
edges.example: setting a 2-year window before deciding the counting unit
edges.resolution_rule: unit definition constrains valid window choices

edges.why_related: counts require correctly resolved citation links and entities
edges.risk_of_conflict: counting on dirty links produces wrong totals
edges.example: unmerged author variants fragment a count
edges.resolution_rule: resolve entities before counting; recount after cleaning

edges.why_related: raw counts are bounded by the chosen citation window
edges.risk_of_conflict: counting without a window yields incomparable totals
edges.example: mixing open-ended and 3-year counts
edges.resolution_rule: window policy fixed before counts are finalized

edges.why_related: field delineation operates on disambiguated entities and citation links
edges.risk_of_conflict: clustering dirty data yields unstable fields
edges.example: duplicate records split a coherent cluster
edges.resolution_rule: clean entities first; rerun delineation

edges.why_related: normalization transforms raw counts using reference sets
edges.risk_of_conflict: normalizing before counts are stable wastes work
edges.example: recomputing MNCS after a count fix
edges.resolution_rule: finalize counts before normalizing

edges.why_related: normalization reference sets are defined by the field delineation
edges.risk_of_conflict: normalizing before fields are set invalidates scores
edges.example: MNCS computed against wrong field set
edges.resolution_rule: fix delineation before computing normalized scores

edges.why_related: h-index is computed from per-paper raw counts
edges.risk_of_conflict: computing h on dirty counts misranks authors
edges.example: h inflated by unmerged duplicate papers
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize counts before computing h-family indices

edges.why_related: self vs external classification needs correct authorship resolution
edges.risk_of_conflict: misresolved authorship misclassifies self-citations
edges.example: co-author overlap missed by bad disambiguation
edges.resolution_rule: resolve authorship before classifying self-citations

edges.why_related: distribution diagnostics are computed on the raw count vector
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing before counts are final misleads
edges.example: skew estimate changes after count fix
edges.resolution_rule: compute counts first; then diagnose distribution

edges.why_related: journal indicators aggregate raw citation counts over a window
edges.risk_of_conflict: computing JIF on unstable counts misranks journals
edges.example: JIF shifts after reclassifying citable items
edges.resolution_rule: finalize counts and window before journal metrics

edges.why_related: aggregation-level decisions presuppose computed article-level counts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: consistent level from a count base
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing levels before counts complicates attribution
edges.example: fractional counting decided after counts exist
edges.resolution_rule: compute base counts; then fix aggregation level

edges.why_related: co-citation links require resolved cited-reference entities
edges.risk_of_conflict: unresolved references fragment co-citation links
edges.example: typos split a reference into two co-cited nodes
edges.resolution_rule: resolve references before building co-citation networks

edges.why_related: coupling needs complete, resolved reference lists per document
edges.risk_of_conflict: incomplete references weaken coupling links
edges.example: missing references drop coupling edges
edges.resolution_rule: resolve and complete references before coupling

edges.why_related: validity assessment evaluates normalized indicators
edges.risk_of_conflict: assessing validity before normalization is premature
edges.example: judging fairness on raw counts
edges.resolution_rule: normalize before assessing indicator validity

edges.why_related: validity rests on a stated theory of what citations mean
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping theory leaves validity unjustified
edges.example: claiming citations = quality without theory
edges.resolution_rule: adopt a citation theory before asserting validity

edges.why_related: benchmark comparisons use normalized indicators
edges.risk_of_conflict: benchmarking raw counts confounds fields
edges.example: comparing departments on raw totals
edges.resolution_rule: normalize before benchmarking

edges.why_related: gaming detection builds on self-citation signals
edges.risk_of_conflict: detecting cartels without self-citation context misses signals
edges.example: high self-citation overlooked in cartel search
edges.resolution_rule: compute self-citation before anomaly detection

edges.why_related: reports must carry validity and responsible-use conclusions
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting before validity assessment misleads
edges.example: publishing a ranking without DORA caveats
edges.resolution_rule: complete validity assessment before reporting

edges.why_related: raw transparency competes with normalized comparability
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-normalizing obscures interpretability; raw misleads across fields
edges.example: stakeholders want simple totals but panels span fields
edges.resolution_rule: prefer normalized for cross-field decisions; keep raw for transparency

edges.why_related: single-number convenience conflicts with validity demands
edges.risk_of_conflict: h-index simplicity invites field-blind misuse
edges.example: ranking cross-field hires by h alone
edges.resolution_rule: validity dominates; forbid field-blind h comparisons in evaluation

edges.why_related: journal-metric demand conflicts with responsible-use limits
edges.risk_of_conflict: JIF-for-individuals pressure undermines validity
edges.example: using JIF in tenure cases
edges.resolution_rule: validity dominates; DORA forbids JIF for individual evaluation

edges.why_related: mean-based raw reporting conflicts with skew-aware statistics
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between familiar means and robust stats
edges.risk_of_conflict: means mislead on heavy tails; medians confuse audiences
edges.example: reporting average citations of a skewed set
edges.resolution_rule: skew diagnostics dominate; report percentiles when skew is high

edges.why_related: legitimate self-citation conflicts with manipulation flagging
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between integrity and fairness to authors
edges.risk_of_conflict: aggressive flagging penalizes legitimate cumulative work
edges.example: programmatic researchers flagged as gamers
edges.resolution_rule: human review dominates; flags require integrity review before action

edges.why_related: proprietary coverage conflicts with open reproducibility
edges.risk_of_conflict: proprietary gives coverage but blocks sharing; open lags coverage
edges.example: WoS coverage vs OpenAlex reproducibility
edges.resolution_rule: reproducibility need decides; document coverage gap either way

edges.why_related: field-scheme choice creates contestable normalization outcomes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between scheme convenience and result sensitivity
edges.risk_of_conflict: results flip with delineation scheme
edges.example: department MNCS changes with reclassification
edges.resolution_rule: robustness across two schemes dominates a single convenient scheme

edges.why_related: scope decisions should be logged in the pipeline first
edges.risk_of_conflict: late scope changes force pipeline refactor
edges.example: adding document types after pipeline build
edges.resolution_rule: capture scope decisions in the pipeline before downstream work

edges.why_related: distribution findings should shape reporting choices
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting means then redoing as percentiles
edges.example: switching to median late in reporting
edges.resolution_rule: decide summary statistics from distribution before drafting report

edges.why_related: open-data snapshots feed the reproducible pipeline
edges.risk_of_conflict: unversioned open data breaks reproducibility
edges.example: unpinned OpenAlex dump
edges.resolution_rule: version open snapshots within the pipeline

edges.why_related: disambiguation quality changes false-positive rate of gaming detection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cleaner entities reduce false cartel flags
edges.risk_of_conflict: poor disambiguation inflates false positives
edges.example: name collisions look like reciprocal citing
edges.resolution_rule: improve disambiguation to lower gaming false-positive risk

edges.why_related: validity findings can trigger renormalization with a better scheme
edges.benefit_of_coupling: closes the loop on normalization quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless renormalization without a stop
edges.example: reclassifying fields repeatedly
edges.resolution_rule: revisit normalization only if validity gap exceeds threshold; stop after 2 iterations

edges.why_related: anomaly findings can trigger re-examination of self-citation policy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tightens self-citation handling when gaming found
edges.risk_of_conflict: re-tuning self-citation rules indefinitely
edges.example: repeatedly adjusting thresholds
edges.resolution_rule: revisit self-citation policy only on confirmed anomaly; stop after policy update

edges.why_related: unstable benchmark intervals can trigger redoing distribution diagnostics
edges.risk_of_conflict: looping diagnostics without convergence
edges.example: re-bootstrapping endlessly
edges.resolution_rule: redo diagnostics only if intervals are unstable; stop after method is fixed

edges.why_related: both are reference-based relatedness measures for science mapping
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them produces wrong front/base reading
edges.example: using coupling where co-citation is meant
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct: co-citation = cited-side, coupling = citing-side

edges.why_related: both are composite citation indicators at different units
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aids choosing the right unit indicator
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying journal metrics to authors or vice versa
edges.example: using JIF as an author metric
edges.resolution_rule: match indicator to its proper aggregation unit

conflict_axes.dominance_logic: use field-normalized indicators for any cross-field comparison; keep raw counts only for transparency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: cross-field evaluation feeds a high-stakes decision
conflict_axes.example: comparing a math and a biology department by raw totals

conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validity and responsible-use principles override demand for a single convenient metric
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: metric proposed as sole basis for hiring/promotion
conflict_axes.example: ranking candidates solely by h-index or journal JIF

conflict_axes.trigger: a citation distribution is strongly skewed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: when skew diagnostics indicate heavy tails, prefer percentile/median over mean summaries
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: mean reported for a set with extreme outliers
conflict_axes.example: quoting average citations where one paper dominates

conflict_axes.trigger: reproducibility is required but proprietary coverage is superior
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility requirement decides primary source; document coverage gap regardless
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: study must be openly reproducible but field is better covered in WoS
conflict_axes.example: choosing OpenAlex over Scopus for a shareable study

conflict_axes.trigger: broader coverage adds biased or low-quality document types
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: unit/document-type policy governs which coverage is admitted; do not inflate counts with out-of-scope items
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: adding predatory or off-topic venues to widen coverage
conflict_axes.example: including non-scholarly items to boost counts

conflict_axes.trigger: self-citation rate is high but possibly legitimate
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: route high-self-citation cases to human integrity review; never auto-penalize on rate alone
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: programmatic researcher flagged as a self-citation gamer
conflict_axes.example: stripping all self-citations from a cumulative research program

conflict_axes.trigger: two field schemes give materially different normalized scores
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: require robustness across at least two delineation schemes before locking normalized results
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a department's MNCS flips under reclassification

conflict_axes.trigger: a deadline pressures skipping validity or reproducibility steps
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: rigor and reproducibility gates override delivery speed for evaluative outputs
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: rushing a ranking report past validity checks

conflict_axes.trigger: a metric from one level is used to judge another level
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: forbid cross-level inference; require level-consistent indicators within any comparison
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: using journal JIF to judge an article
conflict_axes.example: aggregating author h-indices to rate a department

edge_cases.trigger: outgoing references counted as incoming citations
edge_cases.example: a review's reference list counted as its citations
edge_cases.detection_method: compare in-degree vs out-degree of sampled nodes against expectation

edge_cases.trigger: distinct authors merged under a common name
edge_cases.example: two J. Smith authors merged inflating h
edge_cases.detection_method: sample merged clusters and check precision against ground truth
resolution: split merged clusters and recompute h

edge_cases.trigger: citation window unstated or shifts across the analysis
edge_cases.example: 2-year and open-ended counts mixed in one table
edge_cases.detection_method: check that every reported count carries an identical recorded window
resolution: fix and record a single window policy
recount all units under the same window

edge_cases.trigger: normalization uses the wrong field reference set
edge_cases.example: MNCS computed against a mismatched field
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each paper's reference set matches its delineated field
resolution: re-derive reference set from corrected delineation

edge_cases.trigger: mean reported on a heavy-tailed distribution
edge_cases.example: average citations quoted for an outlier-dominated set
edge_cases.detection_method: compute skewness and tail share before accepting a mean

edge_cases.trigger: journal metric used to evaluate an individual
edge_cases.example: ranking a researcher by their journals' JIFs
edge_cases.detection_method: flag any individual-level use of a journal-scoped indicator
resolution: block journal metric at individual level

edge_cases.detection_method: compare self-citation share against field norms before adjustment

edge_cases.example: calling a coupling cluster a co-citation base
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether links are cited-side (co-citation) or citing-side (coupling)

edge_cases.trigger: legitimate tight subfield flagged as a citation cartel
edge_cases.example: a small specialized community flagged as a ring
edge_cases.detection_method: validate flags against known legitimate dense subfields
resolution: raise anomaly threshold and add context
route every flag to human integrity review

edge_cases.trigger: indicators from different aggregation levels compared
edge_cases.example: comparing an article to a journal-level score
edge_cases.detection_method: check that all compared units share one aggregation level

edge_cases.example: an unpinned database export drifts between runs
edge_cases.detection_method: attempt a full rerun and diff against published figures
resolution: pin and version the source snapshot

edge_cases.example: a league table published with no limitations section
edge_cases.detection_method: check every reported indicator has attached caveats
resolution: attach a caveat register to each indicator

workflow.objective: fix citation-unit, document-type policy, and counting rules
workflow.do_first_because: unit definition is the highest-coupling foundation every indicator inherits

workflow.objective: select and characterize citation data source(s) and coverage
workflow.do_first_because: source coverage and bias bound the validity of every downstream count

workflow.objective: deduplicate and disambiguate entities and references
workflow.do_first_because: clean entity links are prerequisite for all counts and networks

workflow.objective: set window, compute raw counts, diagnose distribution
workflow.do_first_because: raw counts and their distribution feed every derived indicator

workflow.objective: compute composite, quality, and relational indicators
workflow.do_first_because: composite and relational indicators depend only on counts and clean links

workflow.objective: delineate fields and compute normalized indicators
workflow.do_first_because: normalization is the precondition for fair cross-field comparison and validity

workflow.objective: assess validity, responsible use, and manipulation risk
acceptance_tests: every anomaly flag routed to human review
workflow.do_first_because: validity and integrity gates must pass before any evaluative use

workflow.objective: define benchmarks and compute stability intervals
workflow.do_first_because: comparisons must carry uncertainty before being reported as rankings

workflow.objective: verify reproducibility and synthesize a caveat-bearing report
acceptance_tests: full rerun reproduces indicators within tolerance
exit_criteria: report approved for the stated decision
workflow.do_first_because: reporting is the last, partly irreversible step and requires all upstream gates plus human review

priority_rationale.notes: root scope; every indicator inherits unit definitions
source choice bounds coverage and reproducibility
clean links unlock all counts and networks
window must be fixed before counting
counts are the base of every derived indicator
common composite indicator with high demand
validity gate before any evaluative use
terminal, partly irreversible synthesis requiring all gates

dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates delivery speed for evaluative outputs
dominance_rules.required_action: block release until validity and integrity gates pass
dominance_rules.example: rushing a tenure-relevant ranking past DORA checks

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value indicator is requested before its prerequisites
dominance_rules.required_action: compute prerequisites (clean links, counts) before the requested indicator

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks evidence grounding
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade to heuristic and cite SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR
dominance_rules.example: quoting a 3-decimal MNCS labeled observed without data

dominance_rules.trigger: results pending QA are proposed for hard lock
dominance_rules.required_action: run validation before any hard lock
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a report before reproducibility verification

dominance_rules.trigger: high-stakes evaluation or anomaly flag arises
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-stakes and integrity cases
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: auto-penalizing an author flagged by the cartel detector

dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding objects; fix schema first
dominance_rules.example: padding near-duplicate indicators to inflate counts
adding commentary that breaks strict JSON output

dominance_rules.trigger: an unsupported claim is asserted as fact
dominance_rules.required_action: attach an eligible source or downgrade the claim
dominance_rules.example: asserting causation between citations and quality

dominance_rules.trigger: a metric is used across aggregation levels
dominance_rules.required_action: forbid cross-level inference; compute at one level
dominance_rules.example: using JIF to judge an individual article

dominance_rules.trigger: a cross-field comparison uses raw counts
dominance_rules.rule: field normalization dominates raw counts for cross-field comparison
dominance_rules.example: ranking cross-field departments by raw totals

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix citation-unit and document-type policy before selecting a database
anti_rework_rules.rationale: source choice depends on what is being counted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a source chosen before units are defined
anti_rework_rules.example: picking WoS before deciding if proceedings count

anti_rework_rules.rationale: disambiguation is tuned to a source's schema
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: cleaning rerun after a source switch
anti_rework_rules.example: disambiguating Scopus then moving to OpenAlex

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve entities and references before counting
anti_rework_rules.rationale: dirty links produce wrong counts and networks

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the citation window before computing counts
anti_rework_rules.rationale: counts are incomparable without a fixed window
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: counts reported without a stated window

anti_rework_rules.rationale: normalization reference sets come from delineation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: MNCS computed before fields are set
anti_rework_rules.example: normalizing against an undefined field set

anti_rework_rules.rule: diagnose the distribution before choosing a summary statistic
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a mean reported before skew is checked
anti_rework_rules.example: quoting average citations on a skewed set

anti_rework_rules.rule: adopt a citation theory before asserting indicator validity
anti_rework_rules.rationale: validity claims need a stated meaning of citations
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: validity asserted with no theory frame

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass validity and responsible-use gates before reporting
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a report drafted before DORA/Leiden checks
a figure that cannot be regenerated

anti_rework_rules.rule: require human review before irreversible evaluative decisions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a hard lock or penalty applied without review
anti_rework_rules.example: auto-flagging penalizing an author without review

action: route to human review with a decision record
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human review completed or item resolved
